first_impression.reaction: Our daughter sent this because the Seychelles is on her list, and Geoff will ask straight away whether it's legal. The first lines answer it: 'It will.' Good. I read it all on the iPad. It's calm, it quotes the government pages and it's honest about hospitals, insurance and the wet season. This time the resort questions include deposits and step-free access, which are the two things I'd have asked about. What still worries me is that there's no Australian office on the islands and the page says the hospitals are limited, so I keep coming back to who looks after us if something goes wrong. And the beach ceremony part confused me.

journey.quote: The Seychelles is on your shortlist, and before you choose a bay or a resort you want to know one thing: will the marriage stand? It will.
journey.reaction: That's Geoff's first question, answered in two words. I can forward this paragraph to him as it is.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in the Seychelles?
journey.quote: Read it together once, before you sign anything with a resort.
journey.reaction: Good advice. Slow down before signing anything. That's what I'd tell them myself.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Take out travel insurance that covers medical evacuation, for the two of you and for any parents travelling with you.
journey.reaction: Thank you for thinking of the parents. Medical evacuation is exactly the cover I'd want for my mother.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Australia has no embassy, high commission or consulate in the Seychelles.
journey.reaction: So the nearest Australian office is in another country. Then who do I ring at 2am if someone is in hospital or a passport goes missing? This makes me want to know who on our side is actually there.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Medical facilities are limited outside Mahé, there is no reciprocal healthcare agreement with Australia, and tourists pay for all care.
journey.reaction: Honest, and I'm glad it's said. But my mother is 88. This sentence makes me lean towards Mahé already.

journey.section: What the Civil Status office asks for
journey.quote: One question to settle early: whether the office accepts certified copies of your birth and divorce certificates, or wants the originals.
journey.reaction: Sensible, and 'keep the answer in writing' is right. But it's one more thing the children have to chase with a government office overseas, by email.

journey.quote: Lodge early, well before the Christmas rush if you plan to marry in the new year.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the kind of delay that costs money. I'll tell her.

journey.section: The banns and a special licence
journey.quote: It is normally issued within two days of the application, and a fee applies.
journey.reaction: A fee, but how much and in what currency? I like to know what we're paying and to whom. 'A fee applies' turns up three times on this page and never with a figure.

journey.quote: If you would like your marriage registered at home rather than at the office, tell the Civil Status office at least a week before the wedding takes place.
journey.reaction: At home? Whose home? We live in Melbourne. I think it means somewhere other than the office, like the resort, but I had to read it twice and I'm still not sure.

journey.section: Who performs the ceremony, and where
journey.quote: Your marriage is registered by the Civil Status office, and a Civil Status Officer travels to you when you marry away from the main islands.
journey.reaction: Now I'm muddled. One paragraph says they both go into the office, this one says the officer travels to them. Can they marry on the beach or not?

journey.quote: Many couples do exactly that, with a long lunch at home for the friends who could not make the flight.
journey.reaction: A lovely idea. It might be the answer for the relatives who can't manage that long a trip.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: Deposits. What is due at each stage, what is refundable, and what happens if weather moves the date?
journey.reaction: There it is. Deposits, refunds and weather, in writing. This is the question I'd have asked first.

journey.section: Ceremonies on the beach, at your resort or on another island
journey.quote: Step-free access. Can older guests and anyone using a wheelchair reach the ceremony space, the reception and their rooms without steps or sand?
journey.reaction: Yes. 'Without steps or sand' is exactly my mother with her walking frame. Someone thought about us.

journey.section: When to marry in the Seychelles
journey.quote: Pack insect repellent, choose insect-proof accommodation and see your doctor about health risks and vaccines before you go.
journey.reaction: Good, it says see the doctor. Mum will want her GP's say-so anyway.

journey.quote: Registered taxis run on some parts of the island, and its hospital clinic provides only very limited treatment, so plan the day with older guests in mind.
journey.reaction: Thank you for being straight. That rules out La Digue for our family, I think.

journey.quote: Most of the inner islands can be reached by ferry, and weather can make boat travel dangerous, so check sea and weather conditions and wear a life jacket.
journey.reaction: Life jackets and dangerous boats. I can't picture Mum on that. Fine for the young ones, not for us.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, payments included, in writing. That's what I want when it's our money.

journey.section: Plan your Seychelles wedding with Wedded Concierge
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing. Good. But Melbourne time is not Seychelles time. Who is looking after things there, on the day?

unanswered_questions: With no Australian office in the Seychelles, who do the couple (or I) ring if something goes wrong outside Melbourne business hours? Is anyone from Wedded Wonderland on the ground on the day? (deferred business detail)
Are our deposits protected if a Seychelles resort or supplier, or Wedded Wonderland itself, fails? Whose name are the contracts in, what language (English or French) and what currency?
Will Wedded Wonderland deal with the Civil Status office, the apostilles and the certificate errands after the wedding, or is that all on the couple? (deferred business detail)
How much are the special licence and Civil Status Officer fees, and are they paid in rupees on the day? (fee amounts deferred)
Can the civil ceremony itself take place on a resort lawn or beach, or must the legal part happen in the office? The page left me unsure.
Will Wedded Wonderland arrange airport and inter-island transfers, including for a guest with a walking frame, and avoid boats where possible? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?
How is the fee charged, roughly what range, and do you receive commissions from Seychelles resorts? (deferred business detail)
Have you planned real weddings in the Seychelles I could look at, and how many? (deferred business detail)
Are there extras or Wedded Privileges for couples who book with you? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: If a resort presents a wedding package, ask whether it covers the civil formalities, the officer's attendance and the certificate errands after the wedding, and ask for that list in writing.
turn_offs_found.why: Not a real turn-off, mostly reassurance. Deposits are now in the resort questions, but nothing says how money paid to an overseas resort is protected, whose name is on the contract or what currency it's in. That's the part of my turn-off about contracts and who is responsible that's still only half covered.

turn_offs_found.quote: Registration is made in the office, with both of you present.
turn_offs_found.why: Repeated three times with the 'register at home' line and the officer who 'travels to you'. I don't mind detail, but on the iPad I couldn't work out whether a beach ceremony is legal or symbolic, and that is the whole picture my daughter has in her head.

would_share_with: My husband, the intro and 'Recognition and registering at home', to settle whether the marriage counts in Australia, plus the 'no embassy' line with 'who do we ring?' written next to it
My daughter, the resort question list (deposits and step-free access), the medical evacuation insurance line and the La Digue clinic sentence, so she picks the island with Nana in mind

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-seychelles&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: It's careful and honest, and 'quotes in AUD' and 'fee in writing' are what I want to see. I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd only go ahead if it's a phone call with a real person who can tell me how deposits are protected, who is there on the day when there's no Australian office nearby, and how they'd get my mother to the ceremony without boats, steps or sand.

top_3_changes: Make the beach question plain in one place: say clearly what 'registered at home' means (a place other than the office, such as the resort) and how that fits with 'registration is made in the office', so a reader knows whether the beach ceremony can be the legal one. Keep it sourced, or flag it for the business if the source doesn't settle it.

Add contracts to the 'Deposits' question in the resort list: whose name the contract is in, in what language (English or French) and in what currency. This is a question to the resort, so it needs no new facts.

Following the 'no embassy' line, add one sentence saying who to contact in an emergency (Port Louis consular contact or Smartraveller's emergency line, if sourced). If sourced, say in the closing that the first step is a phone call and a parent can join.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; on-the-ground support, deposit protection, transfers, paperwork help, fees, commissions, real weddings and Privileges placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details and fee amounts listed as unanswered questions, not penalised or made must-fix

open_questions.question: Do fact_06 and fact_203 together support a plain statement that the civil ceremony can be held at a resort or beach (registered 'at home' with a week's notice)? If not, flag rather than fill. Also, does the source pack hold a consular emergency contact (Port Louis or Smartraveller 24-hour line) to support one sentence after the 'no embassy' line?

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half. Relevance is 3 because the page is a legal how-to written to the couple, though it now mentions parents (insurance) and older guests (access, La Digue clinic).

Likelihood to enquire is 3, up from the Mauritius post, because deposits and step-free access now appear in the resort questions. It is not higher because she wants a phone call first and the page doesn't say who is there on the day (deferred, not penalised as must-fix).
Her mother's age (88) and walking frame come from the persona card's voice samples and the earlier panel, not from the page.
The 3-minute budget covered the full article top to bottom, with the FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
